h: A tramp falls for a blind flower seller and bluffs his way through a drunk millionaire's favor; slapstick that turns suddenly, devastatingly tender.

like.r: Another silent comedy with a stone-faced hero and breathtaking physical gags, but driven by a train chase instead of a love story.
A modern black-and-white silent that borrows the same pantomime sweetness and pairs it with a Hollywood love story.
Another sweet, bittersweet romance between two people from different worlds that knows exactly when to stop.

h: The Tramp gets chewed up by the assembly line and the Depression; a string of inspired gags about machines, hunger and the dream of a small home.

like.r: Chaplin's first full talkie turns the same satirical anger on fascism, with a famous double role and a very serious final speech.
A later, wordless comedy of modern machinery and glass-box offices, more cool and choreographed than Chaplin's tramp.
A funny, sad portrait of a little man swallowed by corporate life, with dialogue instead of slapstick.

h: The Tramp stumbles into the Klondike and is starved, snowed in and lovestruck; shoe-eating, dancing rolls and a cabin on a cliff edge.

like.r: Keaton's film-within-a-film delivers equally inventive silent gags, played with deadpan precision rather than Chaplin's sentiment.
Another silent-era comedy built on one unforgettable set piece of mounting physical peril and a hero who is trying to get ahead.

like.t: The Treasure of the Sierra Madre
like.r: The same gold fever played as a dark morality tale, with greed eating three prospectors from within.

h: Chaplin plays both a timid Jewish barber and a ranting tyrant; broad slapstick mockery of fascism that stops laughing for its closing plea.

like.t: To Be or Not to Be
like.r: Another wartime comedy that makes Nazis ridiculous, lighter on its feet and more cynical about actors and ego.
Another satire that treats world-ending leaders as buffoons, sharper and much blacker.
The Marx Brothers' anarchic take on a dictator-ruled country, all wisecracks where Chaplin leans on pathos.

h: A stone-faced railroad engineer chases his stolen locomotive through Civil War lines; one long, real-train stunt chase staged with astonishing precision.

like.r: Keaton's shorter, stranger reverie about a projectionist who walks into the movie, packed with trick-photography invention.
Harold Lloyd's skyscraper climb is the other great silent stunt sequence, with a more eager and less deadpan hero.
A chase-driven adventure that clearly learned from Keaton, trading Civil War locomotives for lorries and boulders.

h: A movie projectionist dozes off and strolls into the screen; 45 minutes of silent slapstick and trick photography still hard to explain.

like.r: Keaton's longer and more grounded masterpiece, built on a single sustained train chase instead of dream logic.
Another film where a character steps across the cinema screen, with melancholy replacing the slapstick.
A warm tribute to the silent era and its magicians, aimed at younger viewers.

h: Harold Lloyd's go-getter clerk fakes his way up the ladder, then climbs a real skyscraper; the clock-dangling finale is still nerve-wracking.

like.r: Keaton's equally daring silent stunt comedy, with a calmer, stoic hero who never mugs for the audience.
A more sentimental silent comedy about a small man bluffing his way into a better life.
Modern action built on the same principle that the star really is hanging from the building.

h: A runaway heiress and a broke reporter bicker their way across the country by bus; the blueprint for the screwball road romance.

like.r: Screwball at a higher speed and a higher pitch, with a madcap heiress who all but kidnaps the man she loves.
Another runaway-royal romance with a journalist, tilted toward the bittersweet instead of the happy ending.
A glossier, more talkative class-crossing comedy of remarriage with three men circling one heiress.

h: A naive scout leader is appointed senator and walks into a machine of graft; a stubborn civics lesson that still works as a rousing underdog story.

like.r: One principled person arguing against a hostile room, with a single jury room in place of the Senate floor.
The cynical, procedural counterpart: real people exposing Washington corruption without a rousing filibuster speech.
Capra's other portrait of a decent American man against greedy powers, softer on the politics and heavier on tears.

h: A small-town banker on the brink of suicide is shown the world without him; sentimental, darker than its reputation, and built to wreck you.

like.r: Capra's other fable of a decent man against a corrupt system, with a political setting and a stirring finish.
The source of the haunted-by-your-own-life Christmas story, with a miser in place of a good man.
A comedy about a man forced to relive days until he learns to care about the town around him.

h: A buttoned-up paleontologist is swept up by a ditzy heiress, a pet leopard and a lost dinosaur bone; screwball at peak velocity.

like.r: Hawks's other screwball, even faster, with overlapping dialogue in a newsroom instead of a country house.
Another romantic comedy where a confident woman wrecks the stuffy man she loves, with sharper wit and a con-artist twist.
A loving 1970s remake of the formula, with Barbra Streisand in the Hepburn role.

h: A newspaper editor schemes to keep his ex-wife, and star reporter, from remarrying; the fastest overlapping dialogue of the studio era.

like.r: A zanier Hawks screwball that substitutes a leopard and a dinosaur for newsroom cynicism.
Another sharp newsroom film, but a bitter one about how far a reporter will go to get a story.
Another tongue-lashing battle of wits among sophisticated professionals, with the theater in place of the press.

h: Bogart's Philip Marlowe wades through blackmail, murders and Lauren Bacall's flirtations; a plot nobody can follow and everybody loves.

like.r: The source novel carries the same plot, with a darker streak and a Marlowe who sounds even more tired.
Bogart as another hard-boiled private eye in a cleaner, tighter plot about one object everyone wants.
A 1970s update of the Los Angeles detective story, more fatalistic and far less playful.

h: A sheriff, a drunk, a kid and a cranky old man hold a jailhouse against a rich man's army; the ultimate hangout western.

like.r: The film Hawks was answering: the same lawman under siege, but one standing alone while the town hides.
Another group of gunmen coming together to defend a place, with a lighter, more heroic mood.
Hawks's earlier, more dramatic western about stubbornness and a father-son feud on a cattle drive.

h: A tyrannical rancher and his adopted son drive a huge herd north and toward a collision; a western about pride and mutiny on horseback.

like.r: The same tyrant-versus-crew collision at sea instead of on the trail.
The great cattle-drive novel, longer and more sorrowful, with two old Rangers instead of a father and son.
John Wayne again as a driven, obsessive man on a decades-long mission, with a bleaker and more troubling view of him.

h: A drunk doctor, a pregnant lady, a gambler and an outlaw share a coach through Apache country; a western built on its misfit passengers.

like.r: Ford and Wayne again, in Monument Valley, but in color and with a far darker study of obsession.
A mismatched group of strangers stuck together in a western, with much more talk and a lot more blood.
Also a western about a band of misfits, but built around a siege and hanging out instead of a journey.

h: A bitter Civil War veteran spends years hunting the Comanches who took his niece; a gorgeous western that gradually reveals how ugly its hero is.

like.r: Another obsessive loner on a self-appointed rescue mission, transposed to the grimy New York of the 1970s.
A later western that also asks what the violent man in the saddle costs the people around him.
Ford's earlier, lighter and faster western, with the same Monument Valley landscape and very different attitude toward its Wayne hero.

h: A dispossessed Oklahoma farm family heads for California in a rattling truck; a hard, humane Depression road movie that never lets up on injustice.

like.r: The novel is broader and angrier, with chapters on the migration itself and an ending the film softens.
A modern drifting-across-America story with the same empathy for people pushed out of the economy.
Another working-class drama about exploited labor, centered on one man's moral choice.

t: The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance
h: A senator returns for a funeral and tells the truth about the outlaw who made his name; a wistful western about legends and who gets to print them.

like.r: Another late-era western that questions the myth of the gunfighter and what it costs.
A purer, more romantic story of a gunman arriving to protect settlers, with none of Ford's late irony.
Another film told in flashbacks about the gap between a public legend and the facts.

h: A reporter pieces together a dead press baron's last word; deep-focus photography and a nonlinear structure that changed the language of film.

like.r: Welles's second film, a gentler, more mournful portrait of a wealthy family's decline, shot in the same bold style.
Another American empire-builder whose ambition empties him out, with a more violent and mad central performance.
The novel is a slim tale about a self-invented rich man and his hollow dream of a past.

h: A spoiled heir stands in the way of his mother's second chance as his family's fortune fades; Welles's heartbreaking follow-up, studio-trimmed but gorgeous.

like.r: The better-known Welles film, equally ambitious in style and cooler about a man who gets everything he wants.
Another elegant tale of a rich old family, social ritual and the lives smothered by it.
The Pulitzer-winning novel behind the film, a quiet satire of a Midwestern town changed by the motor car.

h: A Mexican narcotics cop and a bloated American police captain collide at a border town; a sleazy, sweaty noir that opens with a famous long take.

like.r: Another noir with Welles in a key role, set in postwar Vienna and just as fond of tilted angles and shadows.
A later and colder noir about a detective in over his head in a corrupt system.
A modern border-country thriller with similar menace and moral rot.

h: An American writer hunts for the truth about a friend's death in rubble-strewn Vienna; zither music, tilted cameras and a legendary entrance.

like.r: Greene's novella, written as preparation for the film, is shorter and stranger than the movie's famous ending suggests.
Another black-and-white noir about loyalty and betrayal among shady men, in San Francisco instead of Vienna.

like.t: The Spy Who Came in from the Cold
like.r: A Cold War story of betrayal in a divided Europe, as tired and ruthless as the Reed film.

h: A retired detective with a fear of heights falls for a woman he's hired to follow; a dreamlike San Francisco spiral about obsessive love.

like.r: Hitchcock's other study of voyeuristic fixation, lighter in tone and tightly held in one apartment courtyard.
A modern dream-noir that echoes the film's split women and its unsettled reality.
A deliberate reworking of Vertigo's story of a man recreating a lost love.

h: A photographer with a broken leg watches the neighbors and suspects murder; pure suspense from one apartment and a lot of curtains.

like.r: A teen update of the same house-arrest-and-binoculars idea, lighter and less ambiguous about its voyeurism.
Hitchcock's more troubled film about watching and fixating, far more romantic and more disturbing.
A surveillance thriller about an expert who listens in and cannot let go of what he thinks he heard.

h: An ad man mistaken for a spy is chased across America by crop duster and Mount Rushmore; Hitchcock at his most playful and suave.

like.r: The earlier Hitchcock wrong-man chase that this film refines, shorter and rougher, with a British flavor.
Another stylish romantic spy caper with Cary Grant that mixes suspense, glamor and one-liners.
A later thrill ride built on the same brisk set-pieces, jokes and globe-trotting escapes.

h: A spy recruits a woman to marry a Nazi in Rio, then falls for her himself; smoldering romance wound around a poisonous teacup.

like.r: Another World War II romance where love and political duty pull in opposite directions.
Hitchcock's other obsessive love story, more psychologically twisted and more dreamlike.

like.t: The Spy Who Came in from the Cold
like.r: A cold look at the human cost of using a person as a pawn in an intelligence game.

h: A shy new bride arrives at a vast English estate where everyone still worships the first Mrs. de Winter; gothic dread in a candlelit house.

like.r: The novel has the same dread but lives more inside the narrator's head, with her unnamed insecurity at the center.
The ancestor of the plain young woman, the brooding master and the secret hidden in a grand house.
A lushly colored gothic romance with a heroine in a decaying mansion and more overt ghosts.

h: A girl idolizes her charming uncle, then realizes he may be a killer; menace seeping into a sunny small-town home, and Hitchcock's own favorite.

like.r: Another film that peels back the surface of a pleasant small town to reveal something rotten underneath, far more extreme.
Another Hitchcock film in which a polished, charming man brings murder into an ordinary person's life.
A charismatic deceiver who wins a family's trust, in a sun-drenched setting.

h: Two strangers chat on a train and one proposes swapping murders; the other brushes it off, and the first insists on his half of the bargain.

like.r: The source novel is bleaker, with a tormented hero who is much less innocent than Hitchcock's tennis star.
Hitchcock's other murder-for-sport film, confined to a single apartment and filmed in near-continuous takes.
Highsmith's most famous study of a charming killer, with an even colder central character.

h: A bored Canadian in London is framed for murder and runs across the Scottish moors, handcuffed to a stranger; the template for the wrong-man chase.

like.r: The source adventure novel is leaner and more male, with no romance and far more hiking.
The big-budget Technicolor remake in spirit, with the same man on the run and a more polished set of set-pieces.
Hitchcock's next British thriller, with the same blend of comedy, romance and espionage on a moving train.

h: A young woman on a European train cannot persuade anyone that the old lady who befriended her ever existed; a brisk comic mystery on rails.

like.r: Another all-star mystery confined to a train, with a more elaborate puzzle.
A very British ensemble murder mystery with the same wit and class comedy.
Hitchcock's earlier British thriller, equally quick and funny, but about a man on the run across Scotland.

h: Two young men strangle a friend, then host a dinner party with the body in a trunk; one apartment, ten shots designed to feel like one.

like.r: Another Hitchcock story of a cultured killer, with more movement and an innocent man caught in his schemes.
Another single-set drama driven by talk, in which a roomful of men argue over a killing.
Another stagebound Hitchcock thriller built on a perfect murder plan and a detective who sees through it.

h: An insurance salesman and a bored housewife plot a murder; hard-boiled voice-over, venetian-blind shadows and snappy dialogue in a doomed romance.

like.r: The short pulp novel behind the film is nastier and more sordid, with an even less likable narrator.
A steamy modern retelling of the same plot, with a sweating Florida in place of 1930s Los Angeles.
Another noir about two lovers killing a husband, from the same Cain school of fatalism.

h: A broke screenwriter moves into the mansion of a forgotten silent star; a venomous, funny, tragic tour of Hollywood's cruelty to its own.

like.r: Another razor-tongued film about a famous actress and the cost of fame, set in the theater.
A surreal descent into the same Hollywood dream factory, with far more mystery and no rules.
A warm musical about the same silent-to-sound upheaval, seen from the sunny side.

h: Two musicians on the run from gangsters join an all-girl band in drag; a farce with perfect timing and a famously cheeky last line.

like.r: Another comedy in which a man in women's clothes learns more about both sexes than he expected.
Wilder's follow-up with the same star, sadder and wiser, with a gentler romance.
Another classic farce of disguise and chaos, in which a cool leading man is flattened by the people around him.

h: A lowly clerk lends out his flat to executives for their affairs until he falls for one of their mistresses; funny and sad in equal measure.

like.r: Wilder's earlier, much darker take on the same corrosive side of the American dream.
Another bittersweet story of two lonely people connecting without quite getting together.
A more restrained story of an affair, where love and decency pull apart.

h: A washed-up reporter turns a man trapped in a cave into a circus; Wilder's bitterest film and an early attack on media vultures.

like.r: Another furious satire on how the media turns tragedy into entertainment.
A modern news-hound who cheerfully manufactures the stories he sells.
Another venomous black-and-white study of press power and ruthless ambition in New York.

h: An ailing barrister defends a charming man accused of murder in a London courtroom; Christie's puzzle plot wrapped in sparring and a last-minute twist.

like.r: A sturdier, more adult American courtroom drama, with a tougher look at what the evidence really means.
Another black-and-white courtroom classic, focused on jurors and doubt instead of cross-examination.
Christie's best-known puzzle, a harder, darker mystery with a closed circle of suspects.

h: Sam Spade and a gang of liars chase a jeweled bird across San Francisco; the hard-boiled detective film at its crispest and most quotable.

like.r: The novel is even more faithful than most adaptations, and just as clipped and cynical on the page.
Bogart again as a private eye, looser and more romantic, with a plot nobody expects you to follow.
A 1970s detective story that carries Huston's director into darker, more modern territory.

t: The Treasure of the Sierra Madre
h: Three down-on-their-luck prospectors dig for gold in Mexico and slowly turn on each other; a parable of greed with a famously sour punchline.

like.r: Another study of a man consumed by the hunt for wealth, as bleak and with an even larger central performance.
Another French-made story of desperate men and a hazardous job in a remote hot place, tenser still.

like.t: The Treasure of the Sierra Madre
like.r: The mysterious novel behind the film, with a similar plot and a more political charge.

h: A gin-soaked riverboat captain and a prim missionary take a rattling steamer down a jungle river; bickering turns into romance and mission.

like.r: A lighter jungle adventure pairing a grouchy rogue with an uptight woman who ends up loving the ride.
Another weary Bogart who is dragged out of his cynicism by a woman and a war.
A faster adventure with the same bickering couple, in a more spectacular setting.

h: A washed-up boxer turned dockworker must choose between loyalty to a corrupt union and his conscience; Brando's raw, mumbling, wounded star turn.

like.r: Kazan and Brando again, in a hot-blooded chamber drama with a more theatrical and more fragile cast.
Another black-and-white film about one man's conscience against the crowd.
A real-life, 1970s version of the lone honest man exposing an institution that wants silence.

h: A fading Southern belle moves in with her sister and her brutish brother-in-law in a sweltering New Orleans flat; a collision that only breaks one of them.

like.t: Cat on a Hot Tin Roof
like.r: Another Tennessee Williams hothouse of lies and desire in a Southern household, with Elizabeth Taylor at the center.
Kazan and Brando again, with a tougher and more public story and a very different feel for tenderness.
A modern reworking about a fallen rich woman pushed into her sister's world, with a similar slow unraveling.

h: A restless son in California's Salinas Valley craves his stern father's love while his brother takes it; James Dean's first star turn and an ache of a film.

like.r: The sprawling novel behind the film covers three generations and the whole Cain-and-Abel story the movie only touches.
James Dean's other great film of a lonely teenager and his stifling parents, set in a suburb with pop-color angst.
Another Dean film and another epic family drama on the American frontier, much bigger and longer.

h: A British officer unites the Arab tribes against the Turks and unravels in the glare; an epic of huge desert vistas and a self-doubting hero.

like.r: Another desert epic about an outsider who becomes a messiah to its people, and what that costs.

like.t: The Bridge on the River Kwai
like.r: Lean's earlier epic, equally concerned with how pride and duty twist a man in wartime.
Lawrence's own long, literary account of the revolt, much more reflective and bleak than the film's hero.

t: The Bridge on the River Kwai
h: A proud British colonel builds a railway bridge for his Japanese captors while commandos plan to blow it up; two kinds of duty collide in the jungle.

like.r: Lean's larger, more sweeping portrait of a driven, divided officer in a distant war.
Another prisoner-of-war story, but a brisk, crowd-pleasing one about outwitting captors.
Another film in which institutional pride and military honor ruin the men under them, much more bleak.

h: A suburban housewife and a married doctor fall in love over tea at a railway station, and decide not to; restraint that aches for ninety minutes.

like.r: Another film in which two married people fall in love and hold back, with sensuous style replacing stiff English manners.
Another British tale of feelings left unspoken because of duty and decorum.
Another wartime-era love story that chooses duty over love, with more action and more flair.

h: An orphan blacksmith's apprentice is mysteriously given a fortune and a place in society; Dickens in shadow, fog and gothic grandeur.

like.r: The novel is longer, funnier and more full of odd people, with Pip's shame and growing up in more detail.
A different Dickens orphan story, played as a big-hearted musical.
Another black-and-white British classic with startling angles and shadow, aimed at adults.

h: A poet-doctor is torn between wife and mistress through the Russian Revolution and civil war; snowbound sweep, balalaikas and long gazes.

like.r: The novel is more philosophical and poetic, with Zhivago's poems and a much looser structure.
Another sweeping, romantic epic that follows a love story through the destruction of a society at war.
Lean's other huge canvas, less about romance and more about a lone man in a vast landscape.

h: A young ballerina is caught between her demanding impresario and her composer husband; a Technicolor fairy tale that turns into a nightmare.

like.r: The modern, much more violent take on a dancer losing herself to her art, clearly in the Red Shoes tradition.
Another Technicolor musical with a long ballet finale, lighter in mood and more comforting in the end.
Another film about a young artist pushed to the edge by a tyrannical teacher, with drums in place of toe shoes.

h: Anglican nuns try to run a school in an abandoned Himalayan palace as the wind and the altitude unsettle them; lush color and rising hysteria.

like.r: The same filmmakers' Technicolor dream of art and obsession, bigger and more romantic.
Another lush, atmospheric story of repressed women overwhelmed by a strange landscape.
Another richly colored, hothouse gothic drama set in a looming house.

t: A Matter of Life and Death
h: A bomber pilot who should have died falls in love and argues for his life before a celestial court; Technicolor heaven, black-and-white Earth.

like.r: Another tender fantasy in which a heavenly being is drawn to earthly love, more meditative.
Another 1946 fantasy in which celestial intervention shows a man the worth of his life.
The pair's even more famous Technicolor film, darker, with an artist's obsession at its heart.

h: French generals order a suicidal attack, then court-martial three random soldiers to cover the failure; trench horror and a very cold trial.

like.t: All Quiet on the Western Front
like.r: The great earlier First World War film, seen from the soldiers' side and sorrowful rather than furious.
A modern First World War film with immersive trench-level realism and a much more hopeful bent.
Kubrick's later film about military madness, using black comedy instead of tragedy.

h: A gladiator leads a slave revolt against Rome; a big, star-heavy epic with real political bite and one famously stirring group declaration.

like.r: Another Roman-era epic with a famous set piece, more religious and less politically angry.
The modern descendant: another enslaved warrior set against a corrupt empire, with sharper action.
The blacklisted writer's novel that the film adapts, with its leftist politics stated more directly.

h: A rogue general launches a nuclear strike and the War Room fails to stop it; Peter Sellers in three roles in a Cold War farce that never lets up.

like.r: The same Cold War accident played with total seriousness, a tense, grim twin to Kubrick's farce.
An earlier satire that mocks monstrous leaders, with more slapstick and less cynicism.
Another absurd war satire in which military logic is a closed loop, based on Joseph Heller's novel.

h: From ape-men to a haunted Jupiter mission and a talking computer; wordless, symphonic, deliberately inscrutable science fiction.

like.r: A Soviet space epic equally slow and strange, less interested in technology than in grief and memory.
A more emotional modern space epic that borrows its scale and its star-gate climax.
Clarke's novel of a human evolutionary leap, built on the same awe at a vast cosmic design.

h: A teenage gang leader enjoys ultraviolence until the state reprograms him; garish, funny and nauseating, narrated in its own slang.

like.r: The novel's made-up Nadsat slang is even denser, and its final chapter is one that the film omits.
The grim prototype of a state that wants to break and remake an individual's mind.
Another British film with a charismatic narrator, a rotten youth culture and a mix of comedy and horror.

h: A professor's obsession with a teenager, played as a black comedy of lies and jealousy, with Peter Sellers breaking in to steal scenes.

like.r: The novel's rich, seductive prose is what makes its narrator so disturbing, and the film cannot reproduce it.
Another black-comic portrait of obsession and delusion told with a poisoned narrator's voice.
Kubrick's next film uses the same dark farce and Peter Sellers in multiple roles.

h: Twelve jurors lock horns in a sweltering room over a boy's life; one holdout and a lot of talk, in a film that never leaves the room.

like.r: Another black-and-white legal drama, with more courtroom time and less of the jury room.
Another film where a single decent man outlasts a hostile room by simple stubbornness.
Another single-setting drama, all about talk and moral nerve, but in a murder-thriller key.

h: A drifting college grad is seduced by his parents' friend, then falls for her daughter; awkward, funny, and set to Simon & Garfunkel.

like.r: The novel is drier and more satirical, with Benjamin more of a blank and the ending far less romantic.
Another dark comedy about a young man and an older woman, stranger and more tender.
Another film about aimless drift and an odd intimacy, with the same unforced awkwardness.

h: A bitter couple host a younger one after a faculty party and drink their way into verbal warfare; Burton and Taylor at their most savage.

like.r: Another film version of a famous American play in which long nights and cruelty reveal what people hide.
A short, modern take on civilized couples falling apart in a single room, much lighter.
Another film about a marriage curdling in the American suburbs, less theatrical and more tragic.

h: A bored waitress and a small-time crook rob banks and become folk heroes in the Depression; sexy, funny, and violent in a way that shocked 1967.

like.r: Another film about killer lovers on the run, more dreamy and distant than Penn's.
Another pair of outlaws who become heroes on the run, with a feminist twist.
The French New Wave crime film that clearly inspired Penn's mix of cool, comedy and sudden death.

h: A reluctant war hero is drawn into running his father's Mafia empire; a family saga of slow betrayals, hushed menace and horse-head surprises.

like.r: Puzo's pulpy novel has more subplots and sex, and Coppola's film is the more polished and tragic of the two.
A faster, more street-level view of the Mafia that deglamorizes the code the Corleones live by.

like.t: Once Upon a Time in America
like.r: Another long, elegiac gangster epic about friendship and betrayal over decades.

h: Michael tightens his grip while the film cuts back to young Vito's rise in Little Italy; a colder, sadder, more ambitious saga of an empire emptying its owner.

like.t: Once Upon a Time in America
like.r: Another sprawling, time-jumping gangster epic with long memories and heavy regrets.
Another film where the pursuit of power slowly hollows a man out.
A taut modern crime saga about loyalty and corruption, quicker and more cynical.

h: A paranoid surveillance expert replays a muffled recording and fears it will lead to a killing; an intimate, claustrophobic portrait of a man who listens for a living.

like.r: Another thriller about a sound technician who captures evidence of a crime, flashier and more romantic.
The photographic inspiration for the film, in which a man finds a possible murder in his images.
Another study of a lonely listener whose surveillance work changes him, in East Berlin.

h: A private eye in 1930s Los Angeles follows a husband and ends up wading into water, family and rot; the modern noir with a famously bleak last line.

like.r: Another sunny-on-the-surface Los Angeles noir full of corrupt cops, a tangle of lies and a savvy cast.
The classic detective story that Chinatown honors and darkens, with Huston himself as the film's villain.
A looser, shaggier 1970s take on Raymond Chandler's detective in modern Los Angeles.

h: A cynical club owner in Vichy Morocco must choose between his old flame and the cause; smoky, witty, and so quotable it is nearly wallpaper.

like.r: Another wartime romance set among spies, more erotic and more suspenseful.
Another postwar black-and-white tale of friendship, love and betrayal in a morally gray city.
Another film in which love and duty collide, handled with British restraint.

h: Hollywood's silent stars stumble into talkies and a chorus girl saves the day; the happiest musical ever shot, with a puddle-splashing title number.

like.r: A modern Los Angeles musical that loves the old studio style, with a more wistful and more grown-up ending.
The dark flip side of the same silent-to-sound moment, in which the old star is destroyed by it.
Gene Kelly's other great Technicolor musical, with a more romantic story and a long dance finale.

h: A Kansas farm girl is blown into a Technicolor land and walks a yellow road with three odd friends; songs, witches and a frightening flying monkey.

like.r: The original book is plainer and stranger, with silver shoes, more episodes and no dream frame.

like.c: Clyde Geronimi, Hamilton Luske & Wilfred Jackson
like.r: Another girl swept into a hallucinatory world of odd characters, in animation.
A much darker fairy-tale journey for a girl, set against real wartime cruelty.

h: A willful Georgia belle claws her way through the Civil War and Reconstruction while chasing the wrong man; four hours of operatic, romanticized Technicolor.

like.r: The novel offers far more of Scarlett's cunning and interior life, and its Lost Cause romanticism is equally evident.
Another doomed love story swept up in the collapse of an old order, with snow in place of plantations.
Another bestselling 1930s romance with an obsessive love and a great house at its center, much more gothic.

h: Romeo and Juliet among rival New York street gangs; fingersnapping choreography, a Bernstein score and a very sad, very pretty ending.

like.r: The original star-crossed lovers, with the gang war replaced by a Verona feud and the music replaced by poetry.
A far lighter and sillier teenage-gang musical, with the same dance energy.
Another big-screen musical romance with a bittersweet end, in modern Los Angeles.

h: A would-be nun becomes governess to seven children in the Austrian Alps as the Nazis close in; big, sweet and nearly impossible to resist.

like.r: Another musical about a magical governess who loosens up a stiff father and his children.
Another big family musical set against encroaching persecution, with a more earthy and more tearful feel.
Another lavish 1960s musical with a famous Julie Andrews stage role and a more witty heroine.

h: A nightclub singer and a visiting writer party in Berlin as the Nazis rise; musical numbers that comment on the story like a sharp-edged chorus.

like.r: The source stories are quieter and more observational, with Sally Bowles as one character among many.
Fosse's own wild, self-lacerating musical about a choreographer's burn-out.
A glitzy, cynical, Fosse-style musical about fame and murder in the Jazz Age.

h: A society heiress's second wedding is crashed by her ex-husband and a tabloid reporter; champagne-fizzy talk and a tricky little game of who loves whom.

like.r: Another 1940 comedy of remarriage, even faster, with ex-spouses squabbling in a newsroom.
Another comedy about a rich woman and a newspaperman, with a road trip in place of a country estate.
Another sophisticated screwball in which a cunning woman toys with a stuffy man.

h: A runaway princess spends one day of freedom in Rome with a tired reporter; scooter rides, gelato and a farewell that knows it is final.

like.r: A runaway-heiress romance with a reporter that ends happily where this one doesn't.
Another film about a single perfect day between strangers, told through conversation.
Audrey Hepburn again, in a glamorous New York romance with more edge and less innocence.

h: A Jewish prince is enslaved by his Roman childhood friend and returns for revenge; galley ships, lepers and a legendary chariot race.

like.r: Another Roman-era epic of a slave rising, more political and less pious.
The modern blockbuster take on a wronged man's revenge in Rome, with sharper action.

like.t: Ben-Hur: A Tale of the Christ
like.r: The 19th-century bestseller behind the film, more devout and more sprawling.

t: The Best Years of Our Lives
h: Three veterans return home to the same small city and find it, and themselves, changed; an unshowy postwar drama with real grace.

like.r: Another 1946 film about a small American city and the people who hold it together, with fantasy in place of realism.
Another story of friends from a small town changed by war, set after Vietnam.
Another look at returning veterans and the people who love them, as intimate and humane.

h: A comedy director sets out to live as a hobo to make a serious film and learns why people need to laugh; slapstick and sorrow in one picture.

like.r: Sturges's other great 1941 comedy, a screwball romance rather than a satire on the movies.
The Coens borrowed the title from this film for their own Depression-era comic odyssey.
Another classic comedy about Hollywood and what the movies are for, in a musical key.

t: To Be or Not to Be
h: A troupe of Warsaw actors uses disguise and bad Hamlet acting to fool the Gestapo; a farce about occupation that dared to laugh in 1942.

like.r: The other pre-Pearl Harbor-era comedy aimed at Hitler, with sentiment where Lubitsch has sophistication.
Lubitsch's elegant political romantic comedy, lighter and less dangerous.
A modern comedy that also finds humor in Nazis while keeping its feelings in view.

h: A marshal on his wedding day waits for a killer to arrive on the noon train as the town turns its back; a western that plays out in real time.

like.r: Hawks's friendlier answer to this film: a lawman besieged, but with allies and a lot of jokes.
Another classic western about a lone gunman, with a warmer mood and a child's eye view.
Another black-and-white film about a lone man standing up for what's right in a room of reluctant citizens.

h: A mysterious gunfighter hires on with homesteaders pressed by a cattle baron; a western seen through a boy's adoring eyes, wide and elegiac.

like.r: The short novel is leaner and told by the same boy, as spare as the landscape it describes.
A much later western that takes apart the gunslinger myth Shane builds.

like.t: The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance
like.r: Another film in which a gun-handler's era ends as the law takes hold, with a more ironic touch.

h: Aging outlaws on the Mexican border pull one last job and stick together; a bloody, slow-motion western about men outliving their era.

like.t: Once Upon a Time in the West
like.r: A grand, operatic Italian take on the end of the western frontier, slower and more mournful.
A later western that also asks what is left of violent men when the frontier closes.

like.t: Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid
like.r: Another 1969 film about outlaws chased by modernity, much lighter in tone.

t: Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid
h: Two likable train robbers can't shake a relentless posse and flee to Bolivia; Newman and Redford banter through a western that turns elegiac.

like.r: The same director, stars and charm applied to a Depression-era con game.
The grimmer, bloodier take on outlaws facing the end of the old West.
Another pair of friends on the run who become folk heroes, with a similar freeze-frame ending.

h: A naive Texan hustler and a sickly con man scrape by in grimy New York; a squalid, heartbroken buddy film.

like.r: The leaner novel gives Joe Buck's loneliness and his past even more weight.
Another portrait of a lonely man adrift in a decaying New York, harsher and more violent.
Another tale of two outcast friends where the weaker one depends on the stronger, with a similar ache.

h: Two bikers with drug money ride east toward Mardi Gras and run into small-town hostility; a loose road film, a rock soundtrack and a grim finish.

like.r: Another loose, restless 1970s drifter drama, more intimate and more dryly funny.
Another dreamy American road film made by the New Hollywood generation, with a killer on the run.
The beat-generation novel of restless American freedom that this film updated for the 1960s.

h: A stubborn veteran on a Southern chain gang refuses to be broken by the guards; Paul Newman's grin, an egg-eating contest and a famous failure to communicate.

like.r: A later prison film about hope and an unbreakable spirit, warmer and more redemptive.

like.t: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
like.r: Another rebel battling a cruel institution, with an asylum in place of a prison camp.
Another film about stubborn prisoners resisting their captors, with a bigger cast and more adventure.

t: In the Heat of the Night
h: A Black Philadelphia detective is detained for a murder in a small Mississippi town, then forced to help solve it; sweat, prejudice and grudging respect.

like.r: Another Southern story of prejudice and justice, seen through a child's eyes and gentler in tone.
A hotter, more explosive look at race in a community, set in Brooklyn in a summer heat wave.
Another detective story set in the Deep South where the investigators are outsiders, more violent.

h: A widowed lawyer defends a Black man accused of rape in 1930s Alabama while his children watch; a warm, moral, child's-eye drama.

like.r: The novel has more of Scout's voice, more summer episodes and more of the small-town rhythm.

like.t: In the Heat of the Night
like.r: A tougher, more adult film about racism in the South, with a detective in place of a lawyer.
Another black-and-white film about justice and individual conscience in a courtroom.

h: A murderous preacher with LOVE and HATE tattooed on his knuckles stalks two children down a river; a nightmarish fairy tale in expressionist black and white.

like.r: The original novel is grim and Southern gothic, with the same chase but more grit and less poetry.
Another black-and-white thriller about a smiling, relentless predator stalking a family.
Another dark fairy tale of children facing a real monster in a time of violence.

h: A desperate press agent does a monstrous columnist's dirty work in neon-lit New York; poisonous dialogue and a nightclub-and-newsroom noir.

like.r: Another corrosive film about the press and how far a reporter will go, set in the desert.
Another acid look at ambition and manipulation in an elite world, with the theater as the stage.
Another New York film about corrupt media power, angrier and noisier.

h: A disinherited young man sets out to murder the eight relatives between him and a dukedom; Alec Guinness plays them all in an Ealing comedy of elegant, deadpan crime.

like.r: Another Ealing black comedy, with Guinness in the mix and a gang of crooks undone by an old lady.
Another macabre farce about murderous relatives, American and much more frantic.
A modern caper with the same arch narration, droll politeness and body count.

h: A detective falls for the portrait of a murder victim and then meets her; a hushed, hypnotic mystery of high-society men and a haunting theme tune.

like.r: Another film in which a man's love for an image of a woman becomes dangerous, with a darker pull.
Another 1944 noir, sharper and meaner, with a murder plot seen from the killer's side.
The source novel is told in several voices and is more of a puzzle, with a different ending.

h: A new kid in town is dared into a car race and falls in with two fellow outcasts; teenage alienation in saturated color and James Dean's red jacket.

like.r: James Dean's other defining performance, in a period drama about a son starved of his father's love.
Another film about doomed teenage gangs and the families that fail them, more romantic.
The literary version of the same restless, alienated teen voice.

h: An adoring young fan insinuates herself into a Broadway star's life and starts taking it over; snarling dialogue and Bette Davis in full flight.

like.r: Another 1950 film about an aging female star and Hollywood's hunger for the new.
A far more feverish modern take on rivalry between a veteran performer and an ambitious understudy.
Another New York tale of ruthless ambition, with a columnist and a press agent instead of an actress and a fan.

h: A gifted young pool shark takes on Minnesota Fats and then the gamblers who want a cut; smoky rooms, hard bargains and a love story that goes wrong.

like.r: Tevis's short novel is spare and more drawn into the hustler's head and pride.
Another look at a pool hustler and his protege, made as a sequel years later.
Another black-and-white sports drama about a talented man whose pride and rage destroy his life.

h: Allied POWs dig tunnels out of a supposedly escape-proof German camp; a big, jaunty ensemble caper with Steve McQueen on a motorcycle.

like.t: The Bridge on the River Kwai
like.r: Another prison-camp film, grimmer and more about pride than escape.
Another all-star wartime ensemble on a mission, rougher and more cynical.
Another long, patient prison-escape story, more a story of friendship and hope.

h: A death-obsessed rich kid who stages fake suicides befriends a 79-year-old who loves life; a macabre, tender comedy with a Cat Stevens soundtrack.

like.r: Another film about a young man pulled out of his stupor by an older woman, more mainstream.
A deadpan comedy of an odd young man and an older companion, with a similar feel for melancholy.

like.t: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
like.r: Another counterculture film about a free spirit against stifling authority.

h: Wisecracking Army surgeons in a Korean War field hospital treat the wounded and torment their superiors; overlapping chatter, gallows humor and a football game.

like.r: Another 1970 satire of military insanity, more surreal and more bitter.
The classic novel of war as absurd bureaucracy, the literary ancestor of Altman's attitude.
Another black comedy that mocks military leaders, with nuclear stakes.

h: Teenagers in a dying Texas town drift through football, sex and the closing of the only cinema; a dry-eyed, mournful black-and-white elegy.

like.r: The novel is rawer and more sprawling, with the town's adults given as much weight as the kids.
Another film about small-town teenagers on the edge of change, much warmer and louder.
Bogdanovich's next black-and-white film, a funnier and lighter Depression-era story of a con man and a girl.
